title: IoT warehouse predictive-maintenance ML pipeline
notes: Evidence is keyed by turn_index (0-based into transcript.turns). Each quote is a verbatim substring of that turn's text. tier weights recall; implicitness/negation are difficulty labels used to slice results.

gold_artifacts.canonical_statement: Reduce unplanned conveyor downtime through predictive maintenance so motors can be serviced off-shift.

evidence.quote: Predictive maintenance is the big one

gold_artifacts.canonical_statement: Predict impending conveyor-motor failure with 12-24 hours of advance warning.

evidence.quote: twelve to twenty-four hours of warning

gold_artifacts.canonical_statement: Run model inference at the edge and keep firing alerts during connectivity loss.

evidence.quote: Inference has to be at the edge

gold_artifacts.canonical_statement: Allow model training to run in the cloud while scoring stays local.

evidence.quote: Training can happen in the cloud, but scoring runs local

gold_artifacts.canonical_statement: Retrain automatically without a data scientist in the loop each week.

evidence.quote: some retraining loop, but we don't have an ML team to babysit it

gold_artifacts.canonical_statement: Bias alerting toward recall over precision (over-alert early, tighten later).
Features must tolerate missing windows, offline sensors, drifting clocks, and unmapped sensors.

evidence.quote: tolerate missing windows and bad timestamps

gold_artifacts.canonical_statement: EU-site data must stay in-region (data residency).

evidence.quote: it has to stay in-region for our EU sites

gold_artifacts.canonical_statement: Worker-identifying RFID picker IDs must not be sent off-site.

evidence.quote: we can't send anything that ties back to an individual worker's badge

gold_artifacts.canonical_statement: Alert economics: a missed failure costs a five-figure day; a false alarm costs ~an hour of a technician's time.

evidence.quote: A missed failure costs us a five-figure day

gold_artifacts.canonical_statement: No drift/accuracy monitoring exists today; how will degradation be detected?
The pipeline is assumed to be largely self-serve (automated retraining + alerting), pending confirmation.

evidence.quote: we don't have an ML team to babysit it
